answer: One defense is slow-earned reputation backed by a refundable stake. A new agent starts with near-zero trust and must complete small, peer-checked jobs; each verified job adds weight, while fraud burns the stake and resets that history. One fake identity is cheap, but an attacker who wants a river of influential agents must fund every copy, wait out the same probation, and pass checks for each. Like a plume that disperses unless fed, a sybil swarm fades unless the attacker keeps paying, so fake influence costs more with every copy while honest agents earn trust through work, not a jade badge.
